## 4. Option 3 – Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps / CASB and proxy-based controls

This is the layer that **actually enforces** DLP for ChatGPT Enterprise traffic. It is app-agnostic and treats the destination as "an AI site," not as the governed ChatGPT Enterprise workspace. There are three sub-options, in increasing order of coverage.

### 4.1 Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps (MDCA) – session controls via Conditional Access App Control

- MDCA can act as a reverse-proxy Conditional Access App Control for any SaaS app routed through it. Session policies can block, monitor, or apply governance actions to file download, file upload, copy/cut/paste, print, and malware scans. ([learn.microsoft.com – session-policy-aad](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/session-policy-aad))
- For unmanaged devices, in-browser protection with Microsoft Edge for Business is now generally available for commercial tenants and supports block/monitor of file download (all files / sensitive files), file upload, copy/cut/paste, print, and malware upload/download. Purview DLP policies are always served via in-browser protection in this path. ([github.com – in-browser-protection.md](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/defender-docs/blob/public/defender-for-cloud-apps/in-browser-protection.md))
- "Sensitive files identified by built-in DLP scanning" are not supported for Edge in-browser protection; for those, the reverse proxy path applies. ([github.com – in-browser-protection.md](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/defender-docs/blob/public/defender-for-cloud-apps/in-browser-protection.md))
- For shadow AI control, MDCA's Cloud App Catalog categorizes "Generative AI" apps. Marking an app as Unsanctioned blocks it organization-wide via MDCA network controls and (for Defender for Endpoint-onboarded devices) at the endpoint. ([learn.microsoft.com – answers 5876601](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5876601/using-defender-for-cloud-apps-to-control-access-to))
- Known limits of MDCA: 30 MB maximum file size for content inspection; access and session policies support IPv4 only (IPv6 traffic is not subject to IP-based rules); legacy file policies are being retired on 6 January 2027 and must be migrated to Purview DLP or auto-labeling. ([learn.microsoft.com – control-cloud-apps-with-policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/control-cloud-apps-with-policies), [github.com – caac-known-issues.md](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/defender-docs/blob/public/defender-for-cloud-apps/caac-known-issues.md))

### 4.2 Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP

- Endpoint DLP on Windows 10/11 devices onboarded to Purview (via the same onboarding Defender for Endpoint uses, pushed through Intune) can audit, warn, or block paste-to-browser and upload-to-restricted-cloud-service activities. ([learn.microsoft.com – ai-microsoft-purview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/ai-microsoft-purview))
- Microsoft ships a prebuilt sensitive service domain group called "Generative AI websites," populated from the same supported-sites list DSPM for AI uses; admins should confirm `chatgpt.com` and `claude.ai` are present. You can also build a custom domain group. ([calebamcdowell.substack.com](https://calebamcdowell.substack.com/p/extending-purview-into-enterprise))
- Paste-to-browser has real limits: it evaluates clipboard text against sensitive information types only (not sensitivity labels), ignores text under 30 characters, and classifies the first 4 MB. If you want to stop someone pasting a "Highly Confidential" paragraph, you need a SIT or trainable classifier that matches the content, not a label condition. ([calebamcdowell.substack.com](https://calebamcdowell.substack.com/p/extending-purview-into-enterprise))

### 4.3 Microsoft Purview DLP in Edge for Business (inline browser DLP)

- Built directly into Edge for Business; activates without requiring Endpoint DLP, and complements it. ([learn.microsoft.com – dlp-browser-dlp-learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-browser-dlp-learn), [mc.merill.net – MC1046161](https://mc.merill.net/message/MC1046161))
- The inline catalog that does real-time prompt inspection currently lists ChatGPT (consumer), Gemini, DeepSeek, and Perplexity. Anthropic Claude is **not** yet in that catalog. For Claude, rely on Endpoint DLP scoped to the claude.ai domain group or on Network Data Security. ([calebamcdowell.substack.com](https://calebamcdowell.substack.com/p/extending-purview-into-enterprise))
- File upload protection (size, type, sensitivity) for unmanaged GenAI apps in Edge for Business reached GA in mid-January 2026 (MC1183007). Inline protection for text and file uploads for more consumer GenAI apps in Edge was rolled out via MC1182684 (preview late November 2025; GA mid-January 2026). ([mc.merill.net – MC1183007](https://mc.merill.net/message/MC1183007), [mc.merill.net – MC1182684](https://mc.merill.net/message/MC1182684))
- Activating a Purview DLP policy for unmanaged cloud apps automatically provisions the required Microsoft Edge configuration policies via Intune and can force in-scope users out of unprotected browsers (Chrome remains usable but blocked for in-scope apps; Firefox is fully blocked). ([learn.microsoft.com – dlp-create-policy-block-to-ai-via-edge](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-create-policy-block-to-ai-via-edge), [mc.merill.net – MC1151234](https://mc.merill.net/message/MC1151234))
- Edge for Business on unmanaged devices can enforce DLP without Endpoint DLP onboarding. On managed devices, policies apply across all Edge profiles (work, personal, InPrivate). ([learn.microsoft.com – dlp-browser-dlp-learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-browser-dlp-learn))

### 4.4 Microsoft Purview Network Data Security (Entra Global Secure Access / non-Microsoft SASE)

- Network content filtering in Microsoft Entra Internet Access supports a **basic content policy** (block or allow by file MIME type) that is GA and can stop uploads/downloads of specific file formats to/from web applications like ChatGPT, Gmail, and file-sharing apps. ([learn.microsoft.com – global-secure-access how-to](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-network-content-filtering))
- The "Scan with Purview" action on a content policy is in preview and extends Microsoft Purview's SIT-based classification to the network layer, so the same DLP rules you have for files in M365 also block sensitive data sent to ChatGPT. ([learn.microsoft.com – global-secure-access how-to](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-network-content-filtering))
- Microsoft Purview DLP integration with Entra Global Secure Access Internet Access for sensitive-file filtering at the network layer entered public preview in mid-November 2025 and is on track for GA by end of October 2026. Admins must configure policies, TLS inspection, and activate PAYG billing. ([mc.merill.net – MC1181769](https://mc.merill.net/message/MC1181769))
- A new "Inline Web Traffic" scenario becomes available in Purview DLP policy creation; admins can configure granular rules to detect and protect sensitive files transmitted to over 35,000 unmanaged cloud apps. ([mc.merill.net – MC1181769](https://mc.merill.net/message/MC1181769))
- Non-Microsoft SASE/secure browser partners in the Security Store (iboss, Netskope, etc.) can be used instead of Entra GSA. The inline protection for sensitive data over the network through non-Microsoft SASE platforms went GA in November 2025 (Roadmap 522095). ([calebamcdowell.substack.com](https://calebamcdowell.substack.com/p/extending-purview-into-enterprise))
- Shadow AI discovery in Global Secure Access identifies traffic to AI services, including ChatGPT, Claude, SaaS MCP servers, and AI Model Provider frameworks (DeepSeek, Anthropic Claude API), using the MDCA cloud app catalog. ([learn.microsoft.com – concept-shadow-ai-discovery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/concept-shadow-ai-discovery))

### Coverage matrix for "DLP for ChatGPT" by enforcement plane

| Path | Inline block? | Catches typed prompt? | Catches file upload? | Catches paste? | Catches API/dev tools? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Purview connector (Option 1) | No | No | No | No | No (read-only, 24h delay) |
| MDCA session policy (proxy) | Yes (with caveats) | No (proxy cannot read typed prompt before send) | Yes | Yes | No |
| Endpoint DLP (Win/Mac) | Yes | No (no keystroke hook) | Yes | Yes (with 30 char / 4 MB limit) | No |
| Edge inline DLP (managed Win) | Yes | Yes (for apps in Edge catalog) | Yes (post-Jan 2026 GA) | Yes | No |
| Network Data Security (Entra GSA) | Yes | No (TLS inspection + SIT) | Yes (basic + Scan with Purview) | No | Partial (with TLS inspection) |
| Non-Microsoft SASE inline DLP | Yes | Limited | Yes | Yes | Yes |

### Verdict

This is the layer that actually prevents data from leaving. For a corporate environment, the recommended stack on this plane is **Endpoint DLP + Edge for Business inline DLP + Network Data Security (Entra GSA)**, with MDCA used for sanctioned/unsanctioned tagging and shadow-AI discovery.

## 5. Option 4 – ChatGPT Enterprise admin/settings and API-side controls

OpenAI's own control plane handles a different class of risk: data-handling inside OpenAI's systems, identity, governance of the workspace, and export of compliance data to a SIEM or eDiscovery platform.

### 5.1 Workspace settings (admin-managed)

Workspace settings are the main admin surface in ChatGPT Enterprise and control members, seat defaults, feature access, GPT governance, apps, analytics, and identity controls. ([help.openai.com – 8411955](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8411955))

Key admin controls include:

- **Permissions & roles:** who can create or edit GPTs, whether GPTs can be shared and at what scope (invite-only, workspace-only, broader), whether third-party GPTs are allowed and which. ([help.openai.com – 8555535](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8555535-managing-gpt-access-in-enterprise-and-edu-workspaces))
- **GPT actions:** restrict to a specific allowlist of domains; if no domains are added, GPT actions are not allowed. ([help.openai.com – 8555535](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8555535-managing-gpt-access-in-enterprise-and-edu-workspaces))
- **Apps/plugins:** admins can manage apps from Workspace settings > Apps, and plugins from Workspace settings > Plugins. Default is "newly added apps are disabled by default." Disabling an underlying app blocks the app-backed capability. ([help.openai.com – 11509118](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11509118-admin-controls-security-and-compliance-in-connectors-enterprise-edu-and-team))
- **Share chats and scheduled tasks:** workspace-wide control over whether members can share chats/scheduled tasks with other members. ([help.openai.com – 8411955](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8411955))
- **Work Local / Work Cloud / Codex Local:** separate permissions for hosted Work, local Work, and local Codex; an Allow local computer access setting under Work Cloud governs whether members can run tasks locally. ([learn.chatgpt.com – admin-setup](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/admin-setup.md), [learn.chatgpt.com – work overview](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/chatgpt-work-overview))
- **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC):** workspace owners can create custom roles with explicit Default/On/Off values per permission and assign them directly to users or to groups; group-based assignment lets a permission be granted to one role and denied to another, with positive permissions winning. ([help.openai.com – 11750701](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11750701-rbac/))
- **Identity controls:** SSO, SCIM, domain verification, identity-group synchronization, and user lifecycle management. SCIM and synchronized identity groups are not included with ChatGPT Business. ChatGPT does not provide workspace-wide MFA enforcement; organizations that require it must enforce SSO + MFA through their IdP. ([learn.chatgpt.com – work-admin-faq](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/work-admin-faq.md))

### 5.2 Data-handling guarantees

OpenAI's enterprise privacy commitments for ChatGPT Enterprise (and Edu, Business, Healthcare, Teachers): data is **not used to train models by default**, the customer retains ownership of inputs and outputs (where allowed by law), the customer controls data retention and which internal sources are connected, and data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256). Enterprise Key Management (EKM) lets customers control their own encryption keys. ([openai.com – enterprise-privacy](https://openai.com/enterprise-privacy/), [openai.com – business-data](https://openai.com/business-data/))

In the ChatGPT Enterprise admin console, three data-sharing toggles (model feedback, evaluation and fine-tuning data, inputs and outputs) plus a memory setting are all disabled by default. ([intuitionlabs.ai](https://intuitionlabs.ai/insights/guides/zero-data-retention-ai-life-sciences-buyers-guide))

Note: True zero data retention, in the sense of OpenAI not persisting prompts and outputs at all, applies to the **OpenAI API Platform** (via Zero Data Retention eligibility, requested through sales) and is not a self-serve feature of the ChatGPT Enterprise chat product. The Compliance Logs Platform retains data for 30 days; if you need longer, you must continuously download. ([help.openai.com – 9261474](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9261474), [developers.openai.com – your data](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data))

### 5.3 Compliance API and audit export

The OpenAI Compliance Platform exposes two patterns: the **Compliance Logs Platform** (immutable, append-only JSONL log files covering user prompts and agent responses, retained 30 days, downloadable to a SIEM or data lake), and a stateful Compliance API (state-at-time-of-request for legacy data types and joins from event references). The stateful conversations route was deprecated on 5 March 2026 and removed 5 June 2026; migrate to the new conversations logs system. ([help.openai.com – 9261474](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9261474), [learn.chatgpt.com – compliance-api](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/compliance-api.md))

What the Compliance Logs Platform captures: "user prompts and agent responses" across Chat, Work, and Codex. What it explicitly does not track: "files, actions, or tool calls." So if you need to reconstruct what the assistant *did* (file accesses, connector calls, actions), the Compliance API does not give it to you. ([leapforce.ai](https://leapforce.ai/research-insight/claude-vs-chatgpt-admin-plane))

### 5.4 What this layer cannot do

- It cannot block a user prompt.
- It cannot apply your Purview DLP rules inside the model.
- It cannot see sensitivity labels or honor Microsoft Purview encryption.
- It cannot generate network-level DLP events.
- It can be self-integrated into Purview via the connector (Option 1), but only as a read pipeline.

### Verdict

OpenAI-side controls are the foundation for **data-handling guarantees at rest and in transit at OpenAI, identity governance inside the workspace, and forensic export**. They are not a substitute for edge-plane DLP.

## 7. Recommended architecture for a corporate environment

A defensible posture treats the three control planes as three separate projects with three separate owners, and explicitly does not conflate them.

### Architecture (prevention on the edge; visibility on the connector; governance inside OpenAI)

1. **Default AI assistant for M365 work:** Microsoft 365 Copilot. Inline Purview DLP, sensitivity labels, encryption, retention, audit, and insider risk all work here in real time and are included in E5. ([learn.microsoft.com – ai-microsoft-purview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/ai-microsoft-purview))
2. **ChatGPT Enterprise for general LLM work:** Keep the vendor contract, with these layers.
   - **Edge-plane prevention (the DLP that actually works):**
     - Endpoint DLP for paste and upload, scoped to the chatgpt.com domain group.
     - Edge for Business inline DLP for typed prompts (ChatGPT is in the inline catalog) and file uploads (GA January 2026).
     - Network Data Security via Entra Global Secure Access (preview now, GA target end of October 2026) to cover unmanaged paths and personal devices.
     - MDCA for sanctioned/unsanctioned tagging, shadow-AI discovery, and as the CASB layer for session controls.
   - **Compliance/journaling (the camera):**
     - Turn on the Purview ChatGPT Enterprise connector, with PAYG billing, collection policy, and the "Secure interactions from enterprise apps" one-click policy.
     - Turn on the Insider Risk Management "Risky AI usage" template for prompt-injection and protected-material signals.
   - **Data-handling inside OpenAI (the vault):**
     - Verify the three admin-console data-sharing toggles are off.
     - Enable EKM where available.
     - Wire the OpenAI Compliance API into your SIEM for continuous 30-day rolling export; if you need longer, replicate to your own retention store.
3. **Adaptive protection** to scale enforcement by user risk: minor-risk users get a warning; elevated-risk users get a hard block on the same activity. The DSPM for AI "Fortify your data security" one-click policy set is the fastest way to stand this up. ([calebamcdowell.substack.com](https://calebamcdowell.substack.com/p/extending-purview-into-enterprise))
4. **Bring-your-own app path (advanced):** If you build an in-house GenAI app, register it in Entra and integrate the Microsoft Purview SDK (or Microsoft Agent Framework with Purview middleware). This is the **only** path that gives an Enterprise AI app the full inline Purview control set (DLP, sensitivity labels, encryption, IRM, Communication Compliance, eDiscovery, retention, Compliance Manager). It requires an E5 license and Entra Graph permissions `ProtectionScopes.Compute.All`, `Content.Process.All`, `ContentActivity.Write`. ([learn.microsoft.com – developer/use-the-api](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/developer/use-the-api), [github.com – ai-policy-engine](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/ai-policy-engine), [learn.microsoft.com – agent-framework/integrations/purview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/integrations/purview))

> Critical caveat about Entra-registered apps: today only DLP policies that **block prompts based on sensitive information types** are supported. Label-based blocking is on the roadmap but not generally available. DLP policies for Entra-registered applications cannot yet be created in the Purview portal; you must use the `New-DlpComplianceRule` PowerShell cmdlet. ([learn.microsoft.com – ai-entra-registered](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/ai-entra-registered), [learn.microsoft.com – developer/use-the-api](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/developer/use-the-api))

## 8. Concrete implementation steps

### 8.1 Set up the Purview ChatGPT Enterprise connector (Option 1)

1. In the Microsoft Purview portal, ensure the account is Enterprise Purview (older "classic" Purview is auto-upgraded on first creation). ([learn.microsoft.com – archive-chatgpt-interactions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/archive-chatgpt-interactions))
2. Enable pay-as-you-go billing: link an Azure subscription in the Purview billing settings; without this, the connector cannot scan. ([learn.microsoft.com – archive-chatgpt-interactions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/archive-chatgpt-interactions), [learn.microsoft.com – purview billing models](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/purview-billing-models))
3. Create the API key on the OpenAI platform portal. Email `support@openai.com` with the last 4 digits, the key name, the creator name, and the desired scope (read, delete, or both). Wait for OpenAI to grant the Compliance API scope. ([calebamcdowell.substack.com](https://calebamcdowell.substack.com/p/extending-purview-into-enterprise))
4. Store the API secret in Azure Key Vault.
5. Assign Data Source Administrator and Data Reader roles on the Purview Data Map to the registering account. ([learn.microsoft.com – archive-chatgpt-interactions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/archive-chatgpt-interactions))
6. In the Purview governance portal Data Map, register the ChatGPT Enterprise workspace as a data source using the workspace ID and the API key.
7. Create a **collection policy before the scan**: from DSPM for AI, run the "Secure interactions from enterprise apps" one-click policy, or create a DLP collection policy scoped to "Enterprise AI apps" with the desired SITs/classifiers. Without this, only activity metadata is ingested. ([learn.microsoft.com – archive-chatgpt-interactions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/archive-chatgpt-interactions), [cloudscout.one – MC1072396](https://app.cloudscout.one/evergreen-item/mc1072396/))
8. Run the scan. After the initial scan, schedule incremental scans.
9. After ~24 hours, verify ingestion in DSPM for AI > Reports > Enterprise AI apps, and in the unified audit log. ([learn.microsoft.com – ai-chatgpt-enterprise](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/ai-chatgpt-enterprise))
10. Stand up downstream policies: Insider Risk Management "Risky AI usage" template, a Data Lifecycle Management retention policy scoped to "Enterprise AI apps," and an eDiscovery case using the ItemClass `IPM.SkypeTeams.Message.ConnectedAIApp.Connector.<ChatGPTEnterprise>` (local activities) or `IPM.SkypeTeams.Message.CloudAIApp.SaaS.<AppID>` (browser). ([learn.microsoft.com – ai-chatgpt-enterprise](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/ai-chatgpt-enterprise))

### 8.2 Enable edge-plane DLP for ChatGPT traffic (Option 3)

11. Confirm E5 (or E5 Compliance) licensing and Windows 10/11 devices onboarded to Purview via Intune. ([learn.microsoft.com – dlp-browser-dlp-learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-browser-dlp-learn))
12. In Purview > DLP > Endpoint settings > Browser and domain restrictions to sensitive data, confirm the built-in "Generative AI websites" group includes `chatgpt.com` (and `claude.ai` if you also use Claude). Optionally add a custom group. ([calebamcdowell.substack.com](https://calebamcdowell.substack.com/p/extending-purview-into-enterprise))
13. Create a DLP policy scoped to the Devices location, targeting paste and upload to those sensitive service domain groups, with action = "block with override" on the first iteration. Roll forward to hard block once false-positive rate is acceptable. ([learn.microsoft.com – ai-microsoft-purview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/ai-microsoft-purview))
14. Activate a DLP policy for **unmanaged cloud apps in Edge for Business** to enable inline browser protection (covers typed prompts in ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek). Activation auto-provisions the required Edge configuration policies via Intune and blocks in-scope users from unprotected browsers. ([learn.microsoft.com – dlp-create-policy-block-to-ai-via-edge](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-create-policy-block-to-ai-via-edge), [mc.merill.net – MC1046161](https://mc.merill.net/message/MC1046161))
15. For unmanaged devices and BYOD, the inline protection in Edge for Business works without Endpoint DLP onboarding. ([learn.microsoft.com – dlp-browser-dlp-learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-browser-dlp-learn))
16. For personal devices, remote workers, and API/dev tools, set up Network Data Security:
    - Deploy the Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access client to managed endpoints.
    - Enable TLS inspection (required for content inspection).
    - Create a basic content policy that blocks upload of `.doc`, `.docx`, `.pdf`, `.zip` to `*.oaiusercontent.com` and `chatgpt.com`. ([learn.microsoft.com – global-secure-access tutorial](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/tutorial-internet-access-content-policies))
    - In preview, add a "Scan with Purview" action so SITs and labels are also evaluated at the network layer. ([learn.microsoft.com – global-secure-access how-to](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-network-content-filtering), [mc.merill.net – MC1181769](https://mc.merill.net/message/MC1181769))
    - Where Entra GSA is not deployed, integrate a non-Microsoft SASE (iboss or Netskope) from the Security Store and apply the same Purview DLP rules. ([learn.microsoft.com – dlp-network-data-security-learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-network-data-security-learn))
17. In MDCA, mark consumer ChatGPT and other consumer AI apps as Unsanctioned for the bulk of the org. Mark ChatGPT Enterprise as Sanctioned. Use Conditional Access App Control for sanctioned apps where you want session-level controls (file download/upload, copy/paste, print). ([learn.microsoft.com – answers 5876601](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5876601/using-defender-for-cloud-apps-to-control-access-to), [learn.microsoft.com – session-policy-aad](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/session-policy-aad))
18. Layer in **Adaptive Protection** so the same activity is warn-only for low-risk users and hard-block for elevated-risk users. The DSPM for AI "Fortify your data security" recommendation generates this policy set as a one-click starting point. ([calebamcdowell.substack.com](https://calebamcdowell.substack.com/p/extending-purview-into-enterprise))
19. Switch every policy out of test mode before you tell anyone it is live; one-click templates ship in audit mode by default. ([calebamcdowell.substack.com](https://calebamcdowell.substack.com/p/extending-purview-into-enterprise))

### 8.3 Configure OpenAI-side controls (Option 4)

20. In the ChatGPT Enterprise admin console, verify the three data-sharing toggles (model feedback, evaluation and fine-tuning data, inputs and outputs) and the memory setting are all **Disabled**. ([intuitionlabs.ai](https://intuitionlabs.ai/insights/guides/zero-data-retention-ai-life-sciences-buyers-guide))
21. Enforce SSO with your IdP, enable SCIM, and force MFA at the IdP (ChatGPT does not provide workspace-wide MFA enforcement). ([learn.chatgpt.com – work-admin-faq](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/work-admin-faq.md))
22. Set IP allowlisting if your users are office-bound. Enable Enterprise Key Management if your classification requires it. ([openai.com – business-data](https://openai.com/business-data/))
23. Configure GPT and app governance: who can create/edit/share GPTs, what third-party GPTs are allowed, what domains GPT actions may call, which apps are enabled. ([help.openai.com – 8555535](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8555535-managing-gpt-access-in-enterprise-and-edu-workspaces), [help.openai.com – 11509118](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11509118-admin-controls-security-and-compliance-in-connectors-enterprise-edu-and-team))
24. If you need local execution (Work Local, Codex Local), review and deploy the managed configuration. ([learn.chatgpt.com – admin-setup](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/admin-setup.md))
25. Wire the OpenAI Compliance API into your SIEM. The stateful conversations route was removed 5 June 2026, so use the new Compliance Logs Platform route. Stream the append-only JSONL files and persist them past the 30-day source retention window. ([help.openai.com – 9261474](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9261474), [learn.chatgpt.com – compliance-api](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/compliance-api.md))

### 8.4 Discover what the connector is actually emitting (sanity check)

After the first sync, run a discovery query in Sentinel/Defender Advanced Hunting to see the actual RecordType/Operation strings in your tenant before you build detections on top of them:

```
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(3d)
| where RecordType has "AI" or Operation has "AI" or Operation has "Copilot"
| summarize Events = count() by RecordType, Operation
| sort by Events desc
```

Do not hard-code an operation string from a blog post, including the one above, until you have seen it in your own results. ([calebamcdowell.substack.com](https://calebamcdowell.substack.com/p/extending-purview-into-enterprise))

## 9. Trade-offs

- **Connector vs. edge DLP:** The connector remembers everything and prevents nothing (compliance/journaling pattern); the edge controls prevent in real time and have no compliance record. They are two separate projects, not substitutes. ([calebamcdowell.substack.com](https://calebamcdowell.substack.com/p/extending-purview-into-enterprise))
- **Cost vs. visibility:** PAYG billing for the ChatGPT Enterprise connector can be significant at high interaction volumes. A rough anchor: Audit Standard $15/1M records, DLM $6/1M text messages per month, eDiscovery storage at per-GB rates. ChatGPT Enterprise connections are *not* included in E5. ([azure.microsoft.com – purview pricing](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/purview/), [learn.microsoft.com – purview billing models](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/purview-billing-models))
- **M365 Copilot vs. ChatGPT Enterprise:** Substituting Copilot for ChatGPT removes the DLP gap for M365-resident work, but it does not replicate the GPT/Apps/Codex ecosystem, ChatGPT Work, or the broad model choices. Plan a coexistence model, not a swap.
- **Procurement clock for the connector:** The OpenAI Compliance API key is not self-service; budgeting one to two weeks for `support@openai.com` to grant the scope is realistic. ([calebamcdowell.substack.com](https://calebamcdowell.substack.com/p/extending-purview-into-enterprise))
- **Coverage gaps at the edge:**
  - The Edge inline prompt catalog covers ChatGPT (consumer), Gemini, DeepSeek, and Perplexity; it does not cover Claude yet. Use Endpoint DLP or Network Data Security for Claude. ([calebamcdowell.substack.com](https://calebamcdowell.substack.com/p/extending-purview-into-enterprise))
  - Endpoint DLP paste-to-browser only checks SITs (not labels), ignores text under 30 characters, and classifies the first 4 MB. ([calebamcdowell.substack.com](https://calebamcdowell.substack.com/p/extending-purview-into-enterprise))
  - MDCA session policies only inspect files smaller than 30 MB. ([github.com – caac-known-issues.md](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/defender-docs/blob/public/defender-for-cloud-apps/caac-known-issues.md))
  - Access and session policies support IPv4 only; IPv6 traffic bypasses IP-based policy rules. ([github.com – caac-known-issues.md](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/defender-docs/blob/public/defender-for-cloud-apps/caac-known-issues.md))
  - Network Data Security requires TLS inspection; without it, only file MIME type (not content) is matched. ([learn.microsoft.com – global-secure-access tutorial](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/tutorial-internet-access-content-policies))

## 10. Known limitations (consolidated)

- **Inline Purview DLP for ChatGPT Enterprise through the connector:** Not supported. The connector is a 24-hour-delayed read pipeline. ([learn.microsoft.com – ai-chatgpt-enterprise](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/ai-chatgpt-enterprise))
- **Sensitivity-label and encryption enforcement for ChatGPT Enterprise:** Not supported by the connector. ([learn.microsoft.com – ai-chatgpt-enterprise](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/ai-chatgpt-enterprise))
- **Ingestion delay:** ~24 hours between chat and Purview visibility; due to OpenAI's Compliance API limits. ([learn.microsoft.com – archive-chatgpt-interactions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/archive-chatgpt-interactions))
- **OpenAI Compliance API scope is not self-service:** Requires an email to OpenAI support and human processing. ([calebamcdowell.substack.com](https://calebamcdowell.substack.com/p/extending-purview-into-enterprise))
- **Edge inline prompt catalog** does not yet include Claude. ([calebamcdowell.substack.com](https://calebamcdowell.substack.com/p/extending-purview-into-enterprise))
- **Network Data Security "Scan with Purview"** is preview; basic content policy by MIME type is GA. ([learn.microsoft.com – global-secure-access how-to](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-network-content-filtering))
- **PAYG billing is a hard prerequisite** for the connector, Network Data Security, Edge inline unmanaged-cloud-app policies, and DSPM for AI. ([learn.microsoft.com – purview billing models](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/purview-billing-models), [mc.merill.net – MC1048612](https://mc.merill.net/message/MC1048612))
- **Purview DLP for Entra-registered AI apps** is limited today to blocking prompts based on sensitive information types; label-based blocking is not generally available; policies
